tasks.title: Height above terrain from AMSL
tasks.statement: GPS shows **{amsl} m** AMSL, and `TERRAIN_REPORT.terrain_height` below the vehicle is **{terr} m**. Find the height above terrain (m).
tasks.solution: h_AGL = h_AMSL − h_terrain. This is the same number as `TERRAIN_REPORT.current_height` and `CTUN.TAlt`; remember the ±10 m database error.

tasks.title: Required climb rate on a slope
tasks.statement: A copter flies terrain items at **{v} m/s** onto a slope with a **{s} %** grade. What vertical speed is needed to hold the height above ground (m/s)?
tasks.solution: v_z = V · grade. At 10 m/s and 35% that is 3.5 m/s, more than the default `WP_SPD_UP` of 2.5 m/s (before 4.7, `WPNAV_SPEED_UP`, 250 cm/s), which is why in the lab the height above ground dropped from 40 to 23.5 m.

tasks.title: Speed limit on a climb
tasks.statement: `WP_SPD_UP` = **{up} m/s**, and the steepest section of the route is **{s} %**. At what ground speed can you fly without losing height above ground (m/s)?
tasks.solution: V_max = WP_SPD_UP / grade. 2.5 m/s and 35% → 7.1 m/s: exactly the speed the flight controller braked the vehicle to by itself in the lab (6.4–7.2 m/s). Set `WP_SPD` for the steepest section. Before 4.7 the parameters were called `WPNAV_SPEED_UP` and `WPNAV_SPEED` and were set in cm/s (250 cm/s = 2.5 m/s).

tasks.title: Rangefinder range with tilt
tasks.statement: Terrain following on a rangefinder at **{h} m**; when accelerating and into the wind the vehicle tilts up to **{th}°**. What slant range will the sensor see (m)? This is the minimum for `RNGFND1_MAX` (m; before 4.7, `RNGFND1_MAX_CM`, cm) with no margin.
tasks.solution: D = H / cos θ. In the lab: 39.85 m at 28.9° pitch → 45.5 m in `RFND.Dist`. A 40 m sensor would have gone OutOfRangeHigh and caused a terrain failsafe.
